ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a cyclohexane ring, one carbon on the ring is connected to an OH group and at the same time is also connected to the nitrogen-containing group on the right. On the right, a C-N single bond connected to N is visible, followed by a nitrogen-nitrogen connection in the form of an N=N double bond; the figure also has curved arrows indicating electron transfer, but the question requires ignoring arrows. Reasoning count: Count according to bonds between non-hydrogen atoms, and count double bonds as two bond units. In the cyclohexane ring there are 6 C-C single bonds; the C-O single bond from the ring carbon to the oxygen in OH has 1, not counting the O-H bond; the C-N single bond from the ring carbon to nitrogen has 1; the N=N double bond is counted as 2 bond units. The total is 6 + 1 + 1 + 2 = 10.

method.method_draft: First describe the image components, then count non-hydrogen bonds. Count the six C-C single bonds around the cyclohexane ring. Add the C-O bond to the OH group, but do not count the O-H bond. Add the C-N single bond from the ring carbon to the nitrogen group. Add the two bond units of the N=N double bond. Disregard all curved arrows. Sum: 6 + 1 + 1 + 2 = 10.
